population.value: 80 adult ICU patients with severe traumatic lung contusion who remained mechanically ventilated for 10 consecutive days and subsequently developed VAP and sepsis (Murray score >4, CPIS >6, SOFA score > 10, excluding GCS)

intervention.value: standard nutrition plus high-dose vitamin D (cholecalciferol 100,000 IU/day for 14 days) (Group B, n=40)

primary_findings.quote: patients in Group B demonstrated significantly faster recovery from lung contusion, VAP, and sepsis, reflected by lower Murray, CPIS, and SOFA scores at both week 1 and week 2 (p<0.05)
primary_findings.outcome: Recovery from lung contusion, VAP, and sepsis (Murray, CPIS, SOFA scores)

primary_findings.quote: Group B also showed significantly shorter durations of mechanical ventilation and ICU stay (p<0.001)
primary_findings.outcome: Duration of mechanical ventilation and ICU stay

primary_findings.quote: a lower mortality rate (10.0% vs. 27.5%, p=0.045)
